question:
Order rules limit blocks new promotions when old ones have expired
When I try to create a new promotion with an order-type discount rule, I get an error saying the number of order rules has reached the limit. However, all of my existing promotions that use order rules have already ended. The system counts rules from expired promotions toward the global limit, preventing me from creating any new promotions.

Promotion creation crashes with internal server error when start date lacks timezone info
Creating a new promotion sometimes fails with an unhandled error. The issue occurs when the start date is provided without explicit timezone information. I expected the system to handle both timezone-aware and naive dates gracefully.

Promotion date validation error shows on wrong field
When I create a promotion with a missing or invalid start date, the validation error appears next to the end date field instead. I expected the error to be reported against whichever field actually has the problem.

Extensions visible without proper permissions
When I query an app's extensions in the dashboard API, I can see all of them even though I don't have manage apps permission and I'm not the app owner. Other sensitive data like tokens and webhooks are properly gated behind those permissions, but extensions leak through to anyone who can view the app.

Extension settings return empty for sidebar mounts
When I query settings for an app extension mounted in the sidebar, I get an empty object instead of my configured settings. Widget extensions work correctly, but other mount types return empty. I expected all extensions to return their full settings.

Webhook event query crashes on null list
When I query an app manifest's webhook subscriptions, the request fails if the list of asynchronous event types is null. I expected it to return an empty list instead of throwing an error.

Webhook delivery permanently failed instead of being retried
When I trigger a webhook through the admin panel, some deliveries show up as permanently failed even though the issue seemed temporary. The system marks them as failed immediately rather than attempting to retry, so the webhook notification never reaches its destination. I expected the platform to retry these deliveries automatically like it does for normal webhook events.

Confusing error when webhook has no matching events
When I trigger a webhook whose subscription query doesn't match any events, the error message displays an empty event type name. I expected a clear indication that the subscription query has no matching events rather than a cryptic error about an unsupported event type.

Triggering a webhook with a Sale ID returns a Promotion object instead
When I use the webhook trigger mutation with a Sale's global ID, the system processes a Promotion rather than the Sale I specified. The returned delivery references the wrong entity, so downstream subscribers receive Promotion data instead of Sale data. I expected the webhook to operate on the exact Sale object I provided.

Tax class not loading for product variants
When querying a product variant's tax class through GraphQL, the field returns null even though the variant's product or product type has a tax class assigned. The same query works correctly for regular products, which show their tax class without issue.

Internal server error when browsing products in a channel without tax configuration
When I set up a new sales channel and forgot to configure its tax settings, customers get an internal server error instead of being able to browse products. The error only happens on channels where the tax configuration is missing.

Default tax rate ignored for a country
At checkout, orders shipped to Germany show zero tax even though I've set up a 19% default rate for Germany in the admin. Other countries work fine. The rate is visible in the configuration page but gets skipped during calculation.

Cannot cancel fulfillment when order contains gift cards elsewhere
I'm trying to cancel a fulfillment for physical items, but the system rejects it because the same order also has a gift card fulfillment. I expected to be able to cancel just the non-gift-card fulfillment independently.

Items not restocked when canceling pending approval fulfillment
When I cancel a fulfillment that is still waiting for approval, the products are removed from the fulfilled count but never returned to my warehouse inventory. I selected a specific warehouse for the restock, but the stock levels did not change after the cancellation. I expected the items to be returned to the warehouse I chose.

Generic error for already-canceled fulfillment
Attempting to cancel a fulfillment that is already canceled shows a vague message that it cannot be canceled, without explaining it has already been canceled. I expected a clearer message indicating the fulfillment is already canceled.

Mutation succeeds silently when passing an empty list
When I call the metadata update mutation with an empty list for the input field, the request completes successfully with no errors, but none of the object's metadata is actually changed. I expected either an error telling me the list must contain at least one item, or at least some indication that nothing was updated. Instead I get a successful response even though my metadata remained untouched, which makes it hard to debug client-side issues where the list might accidentally be empty.

Metadata update reports success even with invalid object ID
When I call the metadata update mutation with an ID that doesn't correspond to any existing object, the response comes back as successful instead of returning an error. The returned item is null, but there's no error message telling me the object wasn't found. I expected the mutation to reject the request with a clear not-found error so I know the ID was invalid.

Product images appear nested inside an extra array layer
When an order contains a product with multiple images, the images field in the notification wraps all images inside one additional array level. A product with three images shows up as a single item containing an array of three images, rather than a flat array of three images. Single-image products display correctly since they use a separate code path.

Order details link missing from custom notification emails
When I trigger a custom notification for an order, the email that gets sent has no clickable link back to the order details page. Other order notifications like the confirmation and fulfillment emails all include this link, but custom ones don't. I expected every order notification to include a way for customers to view their order online.

Product attributes missing for unfulfilled items in fulfillment email
When I partially fulfill an order, the fulfillment confirmation email shows product attributes like color and size only for the shipped items. The unshipped items in the same order display no attributes at all.

Rule event history shows broken rule links after creating promotion with multiple rules
When I create a promotion with several rules at once, the promotion's event history records that each rule was created, but the rule links in those entries are broken — they don't navigate to the correct rule page. The same thing happens when updating multiple rules in a batch. If I create or update rules one by one instead, the event history entries work correctly and link to the right rules.

Deleted rule doesn't appear in activity log
After removing a discount rule from a promotion, the rule disappears from the list but the promotion's activity history shows no record of the deletion. I expected to see a rule-deleted entry logged alongside the other changes.

Promotion end date passes but no event appears in history
When a promotion automatically stops being active after its end date, there is no entry in the promotion's event history recording when it ended. The event only gets logged when a merchant manually changes the end date through the dashboard. Administrators reviewing the history cannot tell why the promotion stopped working.

Checkout fund release timeout ignored for durations over one day
When I set the checkout fund release timeout to more than 24 hours in the payment settings, the system appears to use zero hours instead. Funds for expired checkouts are released immediately rather than waiting the configured duration. The setting works correctly when the timeout is under one day.

Requested countries silently dropped when no shipping methods exist
When I query available shipping methods for specific countries, countries that have no shipping methods configured are completely missing from the results instead of showing up with an empty list. I asked for five countries but only got three back.

Order expiration and freeze period show impossibly large values
When viewing channel order settings, the order expiration time displays millions of minutes and the draft order price freeze period shows thousands of hours. I only configured these for a few hours each. The values appear to be raw time durations instead of the expected unit-based numbers.

App remains inactive after retrying installation
When I retry a failed app installation without explicitly specifying whether to activate it afterward, the installation completes successfully but the app stays inactive. I expected it to be automatically activated based on the default setting.

Cannot retry installation that is stuck in pending state
When an app installation is stuck in pending status, I cannot use the retry function. The system only allows retrying installations that have a failed status, leaving me unable to recover installations that are simply hanging. I expected to be able to retry any incomplete installation.

Export to CSV crashes when a product has a blank date attribute
When exporting products to CSV, the entire operation fails if any product has a date-typed attribute with no value. Products where all date fields are filled export without issue. I expected the export to complete successfully, leaving the date column empty for products with missing values.

Order update webhook fires when just adding a note
When I add a note to an order, the system sends an order-updated webhook even though the order status never changed. My external integration treats this as a real status change and takes unexpected action. I expected either no webhook or a note-specific notification instead.

Error response includes unexpected fields when adding order note
When adding a note to an order fails validation, the error response contains extra fields like warehouse ID and order line references that don't apply to this operation. I expected errors to only include a message and error code, consistent with other order note mutations.

Error response sometimes missing the error code
When adding a note to an order fails, the returned error object doesn't always include the error code field. This makes it hard to handle errors programmatically since clients rely on the code to determine what went wrong.

Error message shows wrong permissions when removal is blocked
When I try to remove certain permissions from a permission group, the system blocks the operation because it would leave other permissions unmanageable. However, the error lists the permissions I am trying to remove instead of the ones that would be left unmanageable, making it impossible to understand what the actual problem is.

Channel changes silently ignored on unrestricted groups
When I add or remove channels from a permission group without restricted channel access, the changes are silently ignored with no error message. I expected to either see the changes take effect or receive an error explaining why the operation isn't allowed.

Users can be removed even when it would leave some permissions unmanageable
When I remove staff members from a permission group while also adding new ones, the system allows the change even if the new members lack certain permissions. After the update, some permissions become impossible to manage because the removed users were the only ones holding both manage-staff rights and those specific permissions.

Payment rejected even though entered amount matches checkout total
When I try to create a payment for my checkout using the exact amount shown as the total, the system rejects it with an error saying partial payments aren't allowed. I verified the amount was correct, yet the validation still failed.

Available quantity ignores click-and-collect warehouse stock when browsing from a specific country
When I view a product page for a country where a collection point warehouse carries the item, the available quantity shown is lower than expected — it doesn't include stock at that pickup location. If I switch to a region with no country filter, the same product shows higher availability including the collection point's inventory. I expected click-and-collect warehouses to count toward available quantity regardless of which country I'm browsing from.

Loading warehouses by shipping zone crashes with an undefined name error
When I query for warehouses associated with a shipping zone, the request fails immediately with a name resolution error. The same pattern works fine when loading warehouses by channel, but this one never succeeds. I expected to get back a list of warehouses linked to the given shipping zone.

Local pickup stock hidden when browsing by country
When a customer filters product availability by country, the reported stock count excludes items available at click-and-collect warehouses. This makes products appear less available than they actually are for local pickup in that region.

Translating a promotion clears its link to the original sale
When I create a translation for a promotion that was migrated from an old sale, the promotion loses its old sale ID. The discount reason then shows as "Promotion" instead of "Sale", and the connection to the original sale is gone. This only happens after running a translation mutation, not when creating or updating the promotion itself.

Promotion translation fails when providing description as a string
When translating a promotion's description by passing it as a plain text value, the mutation rejects the input or stores corrupted data. Other entity translations (products, categories, vouchers) accept the description as a simple string, but promotions require a different format. I expected the promotion translation to work the same way as all other translations in the system.

Apply-once-per-order voucher vanishes when cheapest line changes
I edited a draft order and reduced the quantity of the most expensive item so that a different product became the cheapest. After saving, the percentage-off voucher I had applied to the order disappeared entirely instead of moving to the new cheapest line. I expected the discount to stay attached to whichever line was now cheapest.

Voucher discount not shown when editing draft orders
When I open a draft order that has a voucher applied, the discount value doesn't appear on any line items or in the order totals. The voucher is still linked to the order in the admin panel, but its value is completely missing from the checkout summary while editing. This only happens with certain voucher configurations—other vouchers display correctly. I expected the voucher discount to be visible when editing the draft order, just as it was when the order was originally placed.

Draft order prices don't update when catalog prices change
When I edit a draft order, the line item prices stay at their original values even though the catalog prices have changed since the order was created. I expected the prices to reflect the current catalog prices when editing.

Out-of-stock notifications sent even when inventory remains in other warehouses
When I delete a warehouse that holds stock for a product variant, I immediately receive out-of-stock alerts for that variant — even though other warehouses still have plenty of units available. I expected these notifications to only fire when the variant is truly out of stock across every location.

Warehouse deletion rolls back when webhook delivery fails
I tried to delete a warehouse, but the deletion was rolled back because a webhook endpoint returned an error. The warehouse still exists in the system after the error. I expected the deletion to succeed and webhooks to be handled asynchronously.

Search results missing content from orders with many line items
When an order has a large number of items or related data, searching for product names or SKUs from those items sometimes returns no results even though the content exists on the order. The search index appears to silently truncate expressions when the total exceeds the configured maximum, dropping some fields without any warning to the user. Orders with fewer items search correctly, but larger orders have inconsistent coverage in the search index.

Accent-insensitive search ignored when passing plain strings
I built a full-text search query by passing a plain text string to the search vector, but searching for terms with accented characters like "café" still behaves as accent-sensitive. When I wrap the same string in a Django Value expression, the accent normalization kicks in. I expected plain strings to be normalized automatically without needing extra wrapping.

Search results silently drop some fields
Full-text search queries occasionally return incomplete results, as if certain searchable fields were ignored. This happens inconsistently depending on how many fields are configured for searching. No error is raised or shown to the user—the search just appears to skip some columns.

Malformed IPv6 addresses are silently accepted
Entering an IPv6 address with extra brackets produces no error — the system just strips them and treats the address as valid. I expected the input to be rejected so I could fix the typo.

Telephone URL cleaner leaves percent-encoded characters unchanged
When I pass a telephone URL that already contains percent-encoded characters, the cleaner leaves them as-is instead of decoding and re-normalizing them. The email URL cleaner decodes first before re-encoding, so I expected the same consistent behavior.

Cannot update draft order because channel ID change is always rejected
When I try to update a draft order and include the channel ID in the input (even if it's the same channel the order already belongs to), the mutation fails with an error saying the channel ID cannot be updated on an existing order. I expected that providing the current channel ID would be accepted, or that the check would only trigger when actually changing to a different channel.

Cannot set save address to false without providing a new address
When updating a draft order I set save shipping address to false and do not provide a new shipping address, but the mutation fails with an error saying the save option requires an address. I expected that explicitly choosing not to save the address would be valid even without changing it.

Staff password email crashes with unhandled error
When attempting to send a staff password email notification, the system throws an unhandled exception and the email is never delivered. I was configuring automated notifications for newly created staff accounts. I expected the system to gracefully skip the email when the recipient address is unavailable, just as it does for export success, export failure, and password reset notifications.

Staff order confirmation emails fail when no recipients are provided
When an order is placed and the staff notification fires, the system queues a background email task even if the recipient list is missing from the event payload. The task then fails during delivery because the recipient list is null. I expected the notification to be skipped entirely when there are no recipients configured, just like export notifications handle missing recipients.

Query cost ignores limit multiplier for some fields
I configured a cost map that uses the "limit" argument as a multiplier for paginated fields. For queries where some fields pass a limit and others don't, the validator only counts the limit from the first field — subsequent fields with no limit argument get zero cost instead of their proper default cost. This makes expensive queries with many un-limited fields appear much cheaper than they should be.

Query accepted when cost exactly equals maximum limit
I ran a GraphQL query that I calculated would cost exactly the configured maximum allowed cost, but it was still executed successfully. I expected the server to reject any query that reaches or exceeds the cost ceiling. When I slightly reduced the query complexity, it was accepted as expected.

Expensive queries bypass cost limits when cost map has errors
When the cost map configuration references types or fields that don't exist in the schema, the system reports a validation error but then allows the query to proceed without any cost checking. A malicious or poorly constructed query can completely bypass the cost limit and consume unlimited resources.

Discounted price update ignores dirty flag and recalculates all products
When I trigger a promotion-based discounted price update with the option to only refresh products whose prices have changed (dirty products), the system recalculates prices for every product instead of just the dirty ones. This makes the operation much slower than expected and causes unnecessary price updates across the catalog. I expected only products with a dirty discounted-price flag to be touched.

Stale promotion rule stays attached when swapping to same-discount promotion
When a product variant switches from one promotion to another that gives the exact same discount amount, the original promotion's discount record remains linked to the variant. The displayed price is correct, but the old promotion association is never cleaned up and accumulates over time.

Discounted prices become inconsistent after promotion updates
After running the promotion price recalculation, some products display incorrect discounted prices because the price records are written successfully but the promotion rule associations fail to persist alongside them.

Reserved quantity shows as a decimal instead of a whole number
When I check the reserved quantity for a product at a warehouse, it sometimes appears as a decimal like 10.0 or 12.500000000000002 instead of a clean integer. I expected the reserved quantity to always display as a whole number since items are counted in units.

Company name persists after warehouse deletion
When I delete a warehouse and query its details, the company name field still returns a value from the associated address record. Other address-related fields in the same response handle this case differently and return null. I expected all derived address data to be cleared when the warehouse is removed.

Product variant channel context missing from stock queries
When I query stock information and request the associated product variant, the variant's channel slug is always null, making it impossible to determine which channel the variant belongs to.

JSON concatenation fails during batch updates
When I use the JSON concatenation feature to batch-update multiple records, the operation sometimes fails with a database error about missing parameters. Individual record updates work fine, which suggests the issue is specific to how the expression is compiled for bulk operations.

JSON concatenation ignores NULL values for complex expressions
The helper converts NULL database values to empty JSON objects when using simple field references, but when I use a computed expression or function on either side, NULL values pass through and break the update.

JSON concatenation silently drops data on NULL fields
When I bulk-update a model's JSON field using the custom concatenation expression, records with NULL in that field don't get merged correctly — they stay NULL instead of having new keys inserted. The docs say NULL values should be treated as empty JSON, but it only works when the left side is a simple field reference. If I pass any other kind of expression that could evaluate to NULL, the null-handling logic doesn't kick in.

Subscription operations silently excluded from query identifiers
When I send a subscription operation, it doesn't appear in the operation identifier used for tracing and monitoring. If my request contains only a subscription, the identifier shows as "undefined" instead of listing the subscription field name. I expected all GraphQL operation types to be included in the identifier.

Fetching many nodes at once causes disproportionate slowdown
When I request a large number of nodes in a single call, the response time grows much faster than expected — doubling the number of items makes the query roughly four times slower. I was bulk-loading checkout lines and noticed the performance degradation. I expected the operation to scale linearly with the number of items.

Silently drops IDs that don't match the expected type
When I pass a list of global IDs where some belong to a different model type, the function returns only the matching IDs without any warning or error. I expected either all IDs to be resolved or a clear error listing which ones were rejected.

Category label disappears on type subclasses
I defined a base GraphQL type with a documentation category tag, then created a subclass that extends it with additional fields. When I check the schema output, the subclass shows no category even though the parent type has one assigned. I expected the category to carry through to all subclasses automatically.

Empty attribute filter returns all product variants instead of none
When I apply an attribute filter that matches nothing — for example filtering by a reference attribute with an empty page slug list — product variants are returned in full rather than being filtered out. Other entity types like products and pages correctly return zero results for such no-op filters. I expected product variants to behave the same way and return no results when the filter cannot match anything.

Creating an attribute value with a long name causes a server error instead of a validation message
When I try to create an attribute value whose name exceeds the character limit, the request fails with an internal server error rather than returning a proper validation error telling me the name is too long.

Duplicate value detection is inconsistent for accented characters
When creating attribute values, the system sometimes allows two values that appear to be the same if one uses accented characters and the other doesn't. For example, if an attribute already has a value named cafe, trying to add café is correctly rejected as a duplicate. But if the existing value is café, adding cafe is allowed through. The duplicate check treats these differently depending on which spelling is already stored in the database.

Invalid attribute settings error drops some fields
When I try to create an attribute with multiple properties that don't match its input type, only one error appears in the response instead of listing all the invalid fields. I expected every misconfigured setting to be reported so I can fix them all at once.

Product export filter exports everything instead of filtered set
When I select the filter option while exporting products, the resulting CSV contains all products instead of just the ones matching my filter criteria. I applied a price range filter before starting the export, expecting only those products to be included.

Deprecated tax field still selectable when exporting products
I can still choose 'charge taxes' as one of the fields to include in a product export, even though it has been marked as deprecated. The exported CSV contains a column with no meaningful data. I expected this option to be hidden or at least flagged as deprecated so I wouldn't waste time on it.

Non-staff users can be added as notification recipients
When I create a staff notification recipient by entering an email address that belongs to a regular (non-staff) user, the system accepts it and links that user to the recipient. The UI says only staff users should be eligible, but there is no error or warning. I expected the creation to fail with a message that the user must have staff privileges.

Updating a staff notification recipient fails when email is provided
When I edit an existing staff notification recipient and include their email address in the update request, the system rejects it with an error saying user and email cannot both be empty — even though I'm only providing the email and not clearing anything. This happens every time I try to update a recipient that already exists.

Order discount query crashes when order has no discounts
When querying discounts for an order that has no discounts applied, the GraphQL request fails with an error instead of returning an empty list. Other similar queries for checkouts return empty results in this case without crashing.

Error when querying discounts on an order line with no discounts
When I query discount information for an order line that has no discounts applied, the request fails with an error instead of returning an empty list like it does for order lines that have discounts. Order lines without any discount should return an empty collection, not crash the query.

Promotion rules returned with wrong channel when querying multiple channels
When I request promotion rules for different channels in a single batch query, all results are filtered by the first channel I asked about. For example, requesting rules for promotion 1 in the "US" channel and promotion 2 in the "EU" channel both return US-channel rules. I expected each result to be scoped to its own channel.

Duplicate processing after charging a payment
When I charge a payment through the order management interface, the system appears to process the result twice — the payment status updates redundantly and related notifications fire in quick succession. This only happens when completing a charge, not when authorizing or refunding.

Duplicate refund requests sent when another refund is already processing
When initiating a refund on a payment that already has a refund in progress, the system doesn't detect the existing refund and sends a second request to the payment gateway. This can result in duplicate refund attempts for the same order, potentially causing confusion in the payment processor and incorrect accounting.

Duplicate tax class configurations accepted during creation
When creating a new tax class, the system allows me to add multiple identical configuration lines without any warning. But when I later edit that same tax class, the system rejects duplicate entries. I expected the same validation to apply at creation time.

Zero tax rate rejected as invalid
When I try to set a country's default tax rate to 0%, the system returns an error saying negative rates cannot be created. Zero is not negative, so this seems like a validation bug. I was updating the tax configuration for a country where I want a 0% default rate (e.g., for digital goods in certain regions).

Tax exemption toggle fails with generic error on shipped orders
When I try to manually enable tax exemption on an order that has already been shipped, I get a vague "invalid input" message instead of being told the order can't be edited because it's already fulfilled.

Account update notification skipped for metadata-only changes
When I update only metadata fields on my account, the general account update notification is not sent. I expected it to fire whenever my account is modified, since metadata is part of my account. Third-party integrations that listen for the general update notification miss metadata-only changes.

Account update returns server error instead of proper validation message
When updating my account through the API, I sometimes get a 500 internal server error instead of a clear validation message. This happens when the mutation fails to identify the user context, resulting in an unexpected crash rather than a helpful error response.

Metadata updates not persisted during account edit
When I update my account with new public metadata values, the mutation returns success but the metadata isn't actually changed after refreshing the page. Other account fields like my display name update correctly.

Draft pages missing from admin page list
When browsing pages in the admin interface as a staff member with page management access, several draft pages I know exist don't appear in the listing. Published pages show up fine, but any page still in draft status is completely invisible. I expected all pages to be visible to staff who manage pages, regardless of their publish status.

Page body content doesn't get translated
When translating a page to another language, the body content is always shown in the original language even though I've saved different content for the target language. Only the title translation works—the content fields are editable in the admin but changes don't take effect on the storefront.

Page translations without titles show as numeric IDs
In the admin panel, page translation entries that haven't been given a title yet display their database ID as the label instead of a readable name. This makes it difficult to identify which language each entry corresponds to when managing translations.

Staff users bypass customer-only login restriction
I set password authentication to "Customers only" so that only regular shoppers can log in with a password, but staff members are still able to authenticate with their passwords and keep their full admin permissions. I expected staff logins to be downgraded to customer-level access with no admin privileges.

Account merging skips password requirement
When I set the confirmation mode to require a password before merging my guest account, creating an account still merges my previous orders without asking me to enter my password. I was logged out after placing an order as a guest, then created an account expecting it to prompt for my password to confirm the merge. Instead the orders were merged silently and I never had to authenticate. I expected the system to ask for my password before linking those orders to my new account.

Proxy model instances silently fail type checks
When querying objects backed by proxy models, some valid records disappear from results without any error message. This happens when the database returns instances of the concrete underlying model instead of the proxy model. All instances belonging to the model hierarchy should be included in results regardless of which class they were loaded through.

GraphQL errors when fetching IDs on certain objects
I was querying product and checkout objects through the API and sometimes received errors about being unable to resolve the ID field. The same query works fine for other object types. It seems like the ID resolver crashes intermittently depending on which objects are returned.

Custom fields on channel-context types always delegate to the wrapped model
When I define a field that should resolve from the channel context wrapper itself, it instead resolves from the underlying model object. Fields that depend on channel-specific metadata or context return incorrect values.

Staff access restored after login restriction
When password-based authentication is restricted to customers only, users who previously held staff privileges still regain them after logging in. The system strips staff access during authentication but then overwrites it based on the stored token data. I expected my account to remain limited to customer-level access once the restriction was enabled.

Permission checks fail for specific objects
When I try to perform an action on a particular resource like editing a single order or updating one product, the system denies access even though my account clearly has the relevant permissions for those operations at a general level. The same permissions work fine when checking globally, but as soon as the check is scoped to a specific object, it returns nothing.

Expected: permissions should be evaluated against the specific object, not silently dropped.

Cannot retrieve user by ID after login
After authenticating via JWT, any operation that looks up the user by their numeric ID silently fails and returns no user. The authentication backend's user retrieval method interprets the user ID as an email address instead of a database identifier, so lookups using the standard numeric user ID always produce no results.

Checkout payment stays cancelled after failed transaction initialization
When I try to initialize a transaction for my checkout and the operation fails — for example due to a payment gateway timeout or a validation error — the existing active payment on my checkout gets cancelled but is never restored. After the error, I can't complete the purchase anymore because there's no working payment method left. I expected the original payment to be reactivated if the initialization attempt didn't succeed.

Explicit payment action ignored for gift card gateway
When I initialize a transaction through the gift card payment gateway and specify an action like capture, the system silently overrides it to authorization instead. My specified action is never used, which makes debugging difficult since the API response doesn't indicate the override.

Translation language field returns null for valid languages
When querying translations of products or pages, the language information sometimes comes back as null even though the translation exists and has a valid language code. This started happening after we added a new language to our store configuration. The field is required so it should always return a language display object.

Sale ID in translations points to wrong entity
When I query a sale's translation, the sale ID it returns doesn't correspond to any actual sale I can look up. I was trying to fetch the sale details using the ID from the translation response, but it either returns nothing or a different sale. I expected the ID to point to the sale that the translation belongs to.

Page field returns null for existing pages
When I query a page's translatable content and try to access the related page object, it comes back as null even though the page exists. I expected the page object to be returned regardless of the page's visibility status.

Stock quantity not updated in memory after increasing
When I use the stock increase method to add inventory, reading the quantity field right afterward still shows the old value instead of the new total. The database gets updated correctly, but the instance itself doesn't reflect the change until I reload it from the database.

Inventory count doesn't update after reducing stock
After reducing stock for a product, the remaining quantity doesn't show the correct number. I was processing an order and expected the inventory count to reflect the reduced amount immediately.

Staff member sees empty payment methods instead of permission error when viewing another user's account
When I'm logged in as a staff member and query another user's stored payment methods through GraphQL, I get back an empty list with no error. But if I query the same user's stored payment sources, I get a permission denied error. I expected both fields to behave the same way when I don't have permission to view another user's private data.

Order results change when adding a filter
Querying a user's orders without a where filter returns different results than when a filter is added. The resolver uses separate code paths for filtered and unfiltered queries, which can produce inconsistent order lists.

Staff can't see customer's saved payment methods
When I try to view a customer's stored payment sources as a staff member with management permissions, I get a permission error. The customer can see their own payment methods, but staff managing the account can't.

App responsible for export event hidden behind wrong permission check
When viewing which app performed an export event, the system verifies whether the requesting staff member is the same person who carried out the export, rather than checking if they have permissions to manage apps. A staff member with app management privileges can be blocked from seeing which app ran an export they did not personally initiate.

Export events appear out of chronological order
When I view the history of an export file, the events are not displayed in the order they actually occurred. They seem to follow database insertion order rather than the timestamps on each event. I expected the log to show events in the sequence they happened.

Expected behavior: Events should be ordered by their recorded date/time so the history reads chronologically.

Export event message sometimes missing
When viewing the history log of an exported file, some events show no message even though the API guarantees every event has one. This happens for older export records where the event data was created before certain fields were added. I expected all events in the export history to always display a message.

I select the variants I want to reorder, drag them into the desired sequence, save the changes, and the mutation returns successfully. However, reloading the product page shows the original ordering. I expected the variants to stay in the order I set.

Variant reorder doesn't save
I reordered product variants using the GraphQL mutation, but after refreshing the page the variants went back to their original order. The mutation returned successfully with no errors, so I expected the changes to be persisted.

Updating a menu item's name removes its page or category link
When I edit an existing menu item to change only its name, the page, category, or collection it was previously linked to gets removed. I didn't touch those fields — I just wanted to rename the item. After saving, the menu item no longer points anywhere.
I expected that fields I don't include in the update would stay unchanged, like they do with other entity types.

Plugin notifications fail after menu item update
When I update a menu item, my connected plugins don't receive the update event. Other mutations trigger their plugin events without issue.

Image with one oversized dimension passes size validation
When I upload an image that exceeds the maximum allowed size on only one dimension—for example, 150 pixels wide by 50 pixels tall when the maximum is 100 pixels—the upload succeeds instead of being rejected. Both dimensions need to exceed the limit for the check to catch it, so a single oversized axis slips through.

Raw exception shown when uploading certain images
Uploading a specific image causes a raw exception to appear instead of a clean validation error message. The problem happens with images that have certain types of corrupted embedded metadata. I expected to see a user-friendly error message explaining that the file is invalid.

Fields on webhook control context return null when using default resolver
When querying webhook control data in GraphQL, fields that should come from the webhook control context wrapper (like the sync webhooks permission flag) return null instead of their actual values. The resolver seems to ignore the context object entirely and only looks at the underlying model node. I expected all context-level fields to be accessible through the same query path.

Webhook-controlled GraphQL fields return null
When querying webhook-controlled data, model fields that should resolve correctly are returning null values. The same query works fine when webhook control is not involved.

Translating a promotion rule wipes the promotion's original sale reference
When I translate a promotion rule to another language, the promotion loses its link to the original sale that was converted into it. The old sale reference gets cleared, even though I only updated the rule's name or description. I expected translation operations to have no effect on the promotion's sale history.

Promotion rule description translation accepts any JSON blob
When I submit a translated description for a promotion rule through the GraphQL API, the server accepts completely arbitrary JSON without validating that it follows the expected rich text format. This means malformed or invalid rich content can be stored, causing display issues on the frontend when the content is rendered.

Channel lookup returns wrong or missing data for checkouts
When resolving channel information from a checkout, the returned channel is sometimes incorrect or null even though the checkout clearly belongs to an active channel. The problem appears intermittently, especially when multiple checkouts are loaded together in the same request.

Channel info shows stale data after updates
When I update a channel's settings while multiple checkouts are being processed, some checkouts still display the old channel configuration. Reloading the page fixes it, so it seems like cached data is being served instead of fresh results.

Checkout last change timestamp doesn't update after editing customer note
When I update the customer note on my checkout, the "last changed" timestamp stays the same as before. I expected the timestamp to reflect the time I just made the change.

Webhook fires even when customer note hasn't changed
When I update a checkout's customer note to the exact same text it already has, a checkout-updated webhook still fires. I expected the webhook to only trigger when the note actually changes, so my downstream services aren't processing duplicate no-op updates.

Deleted menu item returns null for nested fields like collection
After deleting a menu item via GraphQL, if the response includes nested fields such as collection or children, those fields are always null even when the deleted item had valid associations. I expected to see the actual linked data in the mutation response.

Deleting a menu item sometimes hangs and eventually times out
When deleting a menu item during busy periods, the request can hang for many seconds before completing or failing with a timeout. This happens more often when other menu modifications are running concurrently, even if they're unrelated items in the same menu tree.

Search index not refreshed when adding attributes to a page type
When I add new attributes to a page type, pages that use that type are not re-indexed for search. Changing the name, slug, or removing attributes does trigger a search index refresh, but adding attributes silently leaves search results stale. I expected any structural change to a page type — including adding attributes — to update the search index for affected pages.

Removing attributes from a page type has no effect
When I update a page type and specify attributes to remove, none of them are actually unassigned. The mutation completes successfully, but the page type retains all its original attributes afterward. I expected the specified attributes to be removed from the page type.

Validation error on attributes when only updating page type name
When I update a page type's name without changing any attributes, the mutation sometimes fails with a validation error mentioning duplicate items in the attributes field. I didn't modify any attributes in this request, so I don't understand why duplicates are being reported. I expected the name change to succeed without attribute-related errors.

Checkout marked as fully authorized before payment completes
I added items to my cart and went through checkout. The payment was still processing, but the checkout already showed as fully authorized. When the payment actually failed, the status didn't revert to not authorized.

Approving a fulfillment fails for partially paid orders
When I try to approve a fulfillment for an order that has received partial payment, the system rejects it with an error saying the order cannot be fulfilled because it is unpaid. I expected the system to allow fulfillment of orders that have received some payment, not only orders that are fully paid.

Order data may be stale after approving fulfillment
When I approve a fulfillment, the order returned in the GraphQL response sometimes shows outdated information — for example, the order status or line quantities don't reflect the current state even though the approval succeeded. I expected the order in the response to be fully up to date after the approval completes.

Cannot delete stuck app installation in pending state
I tried to remove an app installation that has been stuck in pending for days, but the API rejects it saying the status must be failed. Since the installation never completed, it's just cluttering my dashboard and I can't clean it up. I expected to be able to delete any installation I don't need, not only ones that explicitly failed.

Deleting a failed installation sometimes fails with an unclear error
When I try to delete a failed app installation from the admin panel, the operation returns an error saying the installation cannot be deleted because its status is invalid. The installation clearly shows as failed in the interface, so I'm confused about why the deletion is being blocked. I expected the installation to be removed successfully.

Product attribute queries hit the database twice
When loading product attributes, the system runs the database query two times — once to gather attribute IDs and again when building the final result mapping. This causes noticeably slower responses, especially under heavy load.

Storefront-visible product attributes not showing on product pages
After marking a product attribute as visible in the storefront through the admin panel, the attribute fails to appear on product detail pages for regular shoppers. The same attribute displays correctly for staff users with management permissions. I expected all attributes marked as visible in storefront to appear consistently regardless of user role.

Variant selection metadata missing when loading product attributes
When viewing a product's details in the admin panel, the variant selection information for attribute options is not available even though the product uses variant-assigned attributes. I expected to see which attributes control variant creation when editing product attributes.

Plugin search crashes when a plugin has no name or description
When I search for plugins in the admin panel, the search returns an error if any installed plugin has a missing name or description field. The entire search fails rather than just skipping that plugin. I expected the search to still return matching plugins even if some don't have names or descriptions populated.

Plugin status filtering behaves inconsistently
When filtering plugins by their active/inactive status across channels, the filter sometimes fails to match plugins even though their configuration clearly matches the requested status. This appears when toggling whether a plugin should be enabled or disabled in specific channels.

Attribute search not filtering results
When I search for attributes in the page type settings, the search doesn't filter the results at all. It shows all available attributes regardless of what I type in the search box. I expected the list to narrow down to only matching attributes.

Page type details won't load at all when checking page assignment fails
I opened a specific page type in the dashboard to review its settings, but the entire page type information failed to display. Other page types loaded without issue. The problem seems tied to whether the system can confirm if pages are assigned to this type — when that check encounters an error, all the page type data disappears instead of showing with just the assignment status missing. I expected the page type to still render even if the system couldn't determine whether pages exist for it.

Publication date includes time information
When I query the publication date on a page, I get a full date-time value including hours, minutes, and seconds, even though the field is meant to represent only a date. I expected to receive just the calendar date without the time component.

Granted refund status stays stuck in pending after failed gift card refund
I requested a refund for a gift card payment, but the system returned an error (the payment gateway was unavailable). After that, the granted refund still shows as "pending" and never transitions to rejected or any other terminal state. Regular (non-gift-card) refunds update the status correctly even when the gateway call fails, but gift card refunds leave the granted refund frozen.

Refund request fails but transaction stays linked to granted refund
I requested a refund through the admin panel, but the payment gateway was unreachable so the request failed. Afterward, the granted refund shows a transaction item already assigned to it, even though no refund was actually processed. When I try again, the system says the refund is already in progress and blocks me from retrying.

Expected: If the refund request fails, the granted refund should not be linked to any transaction item, so I can retry without manual intervention.

Hard to identify dropped fields in webhook warnings
When webhook payloads are missing expected fields, the warning logs show the bad value and error but don't include the field name. I have to manually search through the schema to figure out which field was silently dropped. I expected the logs to tell me exactly which field failed validation.

Filter descriptions missing for ID-based relationship filters
When building GraphQL filter inputs that include foreign key or many-to-many relationship filters, those fields show no description in the schema documentation even though help text was configured on the underlying Django filters. Regular field filters display their descriptions correctly, but any filter using a global ID lookup is silently stripped of its description.

Updating a checkout line item fails with an unexpected error
When I try to change the quantity of a product in my cart, the request fails with an unexpected error instead of updating successfully. The page reloads and the quantity hasn't changed. I've tried refreshing and retrying but the same thing happens every time.

Catalogue discount price wrong when buying multiple units
When I add multiple units of a product with a catalogue promotion to my cart, the per-unit price at checkout is higher than expected. A product with a flat discount shows the correct reduced price when buying one unit, but the per-unit price increases when I increase the quantity. The discount should apply equally per unit regardless of quantity.

Checkout page loads slowly with many products
When I add products to my cart and proceed to checkout, the page takes a long time to load. The delay seems worse when the products are available in many different regions. I expected the checkout to load quickly.

Webhook notification sent even when app has not changed
When I update an existing app through the API without making any actual field changes, a webhook notification is still dispatched to all subscribers. For example, sending an update request that results in zero modified fields still triggers the app updated event. Downstream systems receive the notification and process it as if real changes occurred, causing unnecessary external calls and confusion.

App update fails with out-of-scope error despite having manage apps permission
When I try to update an existing app through the GraphQL API, the mutation fails with an out-of-scope error even though my account has the manage apps permission. This happens specifically when updating the app's configuration or permissions. I expected the mutation to succeed since I have the required permission level.

Negative percentage discount values are accepted
When creating a promotion rule with a percentage-based reward, entering a negative value like -50 is accepted without any error. I expected the system to reject negative percentages since a discount cannot be less than zero.

Negative fixed discount amounts are accepted without error
When I enter a negative value for a fixed discount, the system accepts it without any validation error. For example, setting a discount of -$5.00 passes validation but ends up charging the customer extra instead of applying a discount. I expected negative values to be rejected.

Mixed predicate validation hides catalogue filter errors
When I create a promotion rule and accidentally provide both a catalogue filter and an order filter, the error message tells me I can't mix them. But any problems with my catalogue filter itself — like invalid operators or missing required fields — are never reported. I have to remove the order filter first, then resubmit to discover those separate issues.
